newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed after setting new high.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed after setting new high.

text.p: Pre-report action again made for an uneven close in CME hog futures after October posted a new contract high, traders said. Pork belly futures pared gains on closing profit taking, sources in that pit said.

October hogs set a new high of 57.475 cents per lb but slipped to close at 57.175 cents, off 0.050 cent for the day. Other months ended 0.525 cent higher to 0.350 lower with active December ending unchanged at 57.150 cents.
Positioning ahead of Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report made for the choppy trade while the firm tone to cash markets provided buying incentive at times, traders said.

Steady to possibly firm cash hog calls for Thursday offset early profit taking. Active pork movement at mostly higher prices encouraged ideas for further strength in cash hogs. Projections that hog supplies will remain under year-ago levels into next year added to support, they said.

Average indications on Friday's quarterly Hogs and Pigs report point to all hogs as of September 1 at 96.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 97.5 percent. Kept for breeding estimates averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94 to 99 percent and kept for market estimates averaged 96.5 and ranged 95 to 98 percent of last year.
But nearbys slipped late on renewed profit taking. Rand Financials notably sold December late, pit sources said.
In hog options, trade remained light with light buying of October 56 and 58 straddles cited early, pit sources said.
Pork bellies ran up for sharp gains following Tuesday's bullish CME out-of-town report before slipping on profit taking to close 1.025 to 0.050 higher with February up 1.000 at 78.500 cents.

Buy stops were touched off in February above 78.800 cents a lb which added to the midsession jump. Rand Financials and LIT bought on the advance, traders said, while Rand turned seller late, traders said.
CME reported a net withdrawal of 1.862 million lbs of frozen bellies from CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago last week, above the high end of early estimates of 250,000 lbs to 1.0 million lbs.
But resistance developed on concern hog slaughter would be large enough to again provide more than adequate fresh supplies, traders said.
"A kill over 365,000 head could hurt this market," a trader said.
After the close, USDA estimated hog slaughter of 367,000 head, above the high end of analysts' estimates for the day.
